status: EVIDENCE DATABASE ONLY. Not wired into any simulator module; no model, threshold, chemistry, frozen dataset or campaign was changed. It records what the open literature does and does not establish about sputter/erosion yields of Hall-channel wall ceramics, for later N/O Hall-channel life work. NO DESIGN-LIFE NUMBER MAY BE DERIVED FROM THIS VERSION (see extrapolation_policy and coverage_matrix: no measured N+/N2+/O+/O2+ yield on BN, BN-SiO2 or SiC was located).
evidence_policy: docs/EVIDENCE.md (CLAUDE.md rules 6 and 10). evidence_level = strength/proximity of the source (1-7). evidence_class = quantity type of the numbers in the entry (measured / digitized / inferred / reconstructed / model-derived / assumed). Unit conversion, digitization or fitting never changes evidence_level; it is recorded in transformation_chain.

scope.purpose: Sputter-yield / erosion evidence needed later for Hall-channel wall life predictions with nitrogen and oxygen ions (atmosphere-breathing propellant), with xenon as the reference projectile.
scope.target_naming_note: 'Borosil' = BN-SiO2 channel ceramic of the SPT-100 (S14 Sec. III); 'BGP' = boron nitride-silicon oxide composition (S06). 'M26' is used only as the grade label of the task and of abep_sim/materials.py ('M26/Borosil-class'); no source read here gives the M26 composition (verify). No yield entry is for an M26-labelled sample.
scope.out_of_scope: Gridded-ion-optics metals (Mo, C grids), cathode materials, intake/compressor surfaces, neutral atomic-oxygen erosion of spacecraft surfaces (abep_sim/aochem.py). The Hall-transport uncertainty of CLAUDE.md item 1 is not touched.

scope_rules_followed: published / openly accessible sources only; no contact with any person or lab; no e-mail

no paywall or bot-challenge bypass: pubs.aip.org (Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge), mdpi.com (HTTP 403), sciencedirect.com (HTTP 403), apps.dtic.mil (HTTP 403 to automated fetch), SPIE (closed) were NOT circumvented; those sources are cited at abstract/metadata level with values marked TBD
numbers transcribed only from documents actually read; anything recalled from memory is marked 'verify'
downloaded PDFs kept in the session scratchpad only (not committed); their sha256 is recorded per source so the owner can confirm identity

units_and_conventions.volumetric_yield: mm3/C = volume of target removed per coulomb of incident singly charged ions. Preferred by the EP sputter literature for multi-component ceramics because 'atoms/ion' is ill-defined under preferential sputtering (Tartz et al. IEPC-2009-240, Sec. IV). Converting to atoms/ion needs the material density and the sputtered-species composition, both grade-specific; no such conversion is made here.
units_and_conventions.atomic_yield: atoms/ion = sputtered target atoms per incident projectile (TRIM.SP tables of Eckstein IPP 9/132).
units_and_conventions.erosion_rate_britton: Britton et al. (NASA/TM-2002-211837) report erosion rate in Angstrom/(s * mA/cm2). Exact unit arithmetic: 1 Angstrom/(s * mA/cm2) = 1e-2 mm3/C (our transformation).
units_and_conventions.angle: Incidence angle beta measured from the surface normal unless stated. Britton et al. use theta measured from the surface plane (their Fig. 5); converted as beta = 90 deg - theta (our transformation, checked against their Fig. 5 drawing).
units_and_conventions.QCM_condensable: Quartz-crystal-microbalance yields register only condensable products (B-containing species for BN); the source papers convert to full BN yield with Y_BN = Y_QCM (M_B + M_N)/M_B (Rubin et al. IEPC-2009-042 Eq. 1), i.e. a factor ~2.30 (our arithmetic check of their Table 1 ratios: 2.29-2.30).
units_and_conventions.number_precision: Values are stored as JSON numbers, which cannot keep printed trailing zeros (e.g. a printed 0.0170 or 3.50 is stored as 0.017 or 3.5). The numeric value is exact; the printed significant figures are in the cited table (source_locator).

hard_statements.solver_wall_flux_is_not_an_erosion_predi: The Hall solver's wall ion flux (hall_map_schema_v1 'wall_ion_flux_m2s' / 'wall_ion_energy_eV', re-evaluated in hallthruster_bridge/bridge_lib.jl wall_ion_metrics from HallThruster.jl's WallSheath model: Gamma_i = loss_scale * h * sum_s n_s sqrt(Z_s e T_e / m_s), impact energy Z phi_s + T_e/2, axial ion kinetic energy and incidence angle excluded) is a model-derived Bohm-flux closure. It is NOT a validated erosion prediction: (1) it has never been compared with a measured wall erosion profile in this project; (2) with ion_wall_losses=false the flux is not even removed from the ion fluid (schema 'wall_ion_basis'); (3) 'wall_life_trustworthy' (converged AND sustained AND ion_wall_losses=true AND WallSheath AND unshielded) certifies dynamic self-consistency of the flux inside the solve, not agreement with erosion data; (4) the 1-D solver carries no radial resolution, no magnetic-field-line incidence geometry and no ion energy/angle distribution at the wall; (5) the anomalous-transport closure that sets the plasma state is not identified (CLAUDE.md gate 3 FAIL; credible set empty). Multiplying that flux by any yield in this database produces a sensitivity number, never a life prediction.
hard_statements.screening_candidates_not_for_design_life: The nine ScaledGaussianBohm screening candidates (sgb-screen-01..09) are not admitted transport-ensemble members (credible set = empty per CLAUDE.md item 1 and the gate-3 row of the gate table). Per CLAUDE.md item 1 they never produce design Hall maps and never enter the architecture trade or UQ. Their wall flux/energy fields MUST NOT be used for design life, erosion budgets, wall-thickness sizing or any Vyovrinda design decision.
hard_statements.no_design_life_from_this_version: No N/O design-life or erosion-rate number is supported by this database version: no measured N+, N2+, O+ or O2+ yield on BN, BN-SiO2 or SiC was located, and the only located N/O measurement on a candidate ceramic (Espy et al. 1993, Al2O3 thin films, 50-200 eV) is closed-access with values TBD.
hard_statements.in_repo_priors_not_endorsed: abep_sim/materials.py sputter_Eth_eV / sputter_Y300 (tagged 'literature-class prior', no citation) and the erosion paths that use them (superseded 0-D HallChannel in abep_sim/plasma_devices.py; life.py defaults) are NOT supported or validated by this database. See in_repo_audit.

extrapolation_policy.principle: A yield may be used without a flag only for the same projectile, the same target material class and grade family, inside the entry's energy_range_eV and measured incidence angles, at a surface temperature inside the measured range. Every other use carries one or more flags below, and any flagged result is OUT_OF_DOMAIN: sensitivity or bracketing only, never a design-life, erosion-budget or wall-thickness number. No silent fallback: a consumer asking for a projectile/target pair with no entry must raise, not substitute xenon data, a proxy target or the abep_sim/materials.py priors.

flags.E_BELOW_MEASURED: impact energy below the entry's energy_range_eV.min. Near-threshold behaviour is not constrained: published Xe->BN thresholds span 18.3 eV (MD fit, Yim 2008) to 57 eV (Zhang fit, Rubin 2009), and models of borosil used 30-70 eV (Cheng & Martinez-Sanchez 2007 Table 1). Must be bracketed with several thresholds, never a single fitted curve.
flags.E_ABOVE_MEASURED: impact energy above energy_range_eV.max. Note Ranjan et al. 2016 (abstract) report a sudden jump in Xe->BN and BN-SiO2 yields above 500 eV, so trends need not continue.
flags.ANGLE_OUTSIDE_MEASURED: incidence angle outside the measured set. Ceramic angular dependence is roughness-controlled and flatter than smooth-surface theory (Garnier 1999 abstract; Tondu 2011 Sec. V); smooth-surface fits (Yamamura, Wei) are not transferable to an eroded, roughened channel wall.
flags.PROJECTILE_PROXY: yield measured with a different projectile (e.g. Xe+ data applied to N+, N2+, O+ or O2+). Mass ratio, energy transfer, chemical reactivity (O oxidizes B, Si, C; N is a lattice constituent of BN) and implantation all differ. Forbidden for design life. The energy-transfer-factor scaling used in abep_sim/archengine.py for Mo grids is an assumption of this kind (evidence level 7).
flags.TARGET_PROXY: yield measured/computed on a different material or grade (elemental B, B2O3, C, SiO2 constituent, another BN grade or binder). Grade matters: Rubin 2009 HP vs HBC differ up to ~1.8x at 250 eV within one laboratory; across laboratories (grade and lab confounded) Tartz 2009 Ca-borate-bound BN vs Rubin 2009 HBC differ 4.6-11.8x and vs Rubin 2009 HP (also Ca-borate-bound) 12.2-12.8x at the same energy (our arithmetic from transcribed values).
flags.TEMPERATURE_OUTSIDE_MEASURED: wall temperature outside the measured range. Xe->BN yields rise from ~520 C (Rubin 2009 Fig. 14, preliminary); MD predicts ~2x between 423 K and 850 K (Yim 2008); Passet et al. 2024 (abstract) attribute a 50-60 % under-prediction of SPT-100 exit erosion to a stronger temperature dependence.
flags.MOLECULAR_ION_ASSUMPTION: treating N2+ / O2+ as two atoms each carrying half the ion energy is an ASSUMPTION (evidence level 7, verify). It is common practice in the sputtering literature (recalled, not source-checked here: verify) but has not been checked against molecular-ion data for any candidate ceramic in this database. Espy et al. 1993 used O+, O2+, N+ and N2+ beams at 50-200 eV on Al and Al2O3 (abstract/title only); whether it reports a matched-energy-per-atom molecular-vs-atomic comparison is INFERRED from the abstract, not read (verify). Values TBD; it is the first place to look.
flags.SURFACE_STATE: fluence-dependent surface state not represented: preferential sputtering, Xe/N/O implantation, oxidation of BN to a B2O3-bearing surface (abep_sim/aochem.py note: 'slight B2O3 surface glass'), SiC passivation, roughening, grain detachment (Tondu 2011), moisture uptake of BN (Topper 2011; Tartz 2009; Abashkin 2007). TRIM.SP entries are 'only low fluence' (Eckstein IPP 9/132).
flags.NEUTRALIZATION_STATE: yield measured with a neutralization/surface-potential condition that differs from a floating Hall-channel wall. Topper 2011 / Rubin 2009 found BN yields rise ~2x with aggressive plasma-bridge neutralization; Nikiporetz 2007 found no difference up to +30 V surface potential (Xe plasma on Si3N4+BN); Tondu 2011 attributes an alumina discrepancy to surface bias. Treated as a systematic uncertainty of order 2x for insulators.
flags.VALUES_TBD: entry exists but its numbers were not accessed (closed access or bot challenge); it can only motivate a test plan, never be used numerically.

extrapolation_policy.result_status_rule: result_status = IN_DOMAIN only if the flag set is empty AND the entry evidence_class is measured (or a fit whose fit_domain covers the query); else OUT_OF_DOMAIN. An OUT_OF_DOMAIN erosion estimate may appear only in sensitivity/bracketing tables labelled as such, and never feeds a trade, UQ envelope or life margin as if it were a prediction.
extrapolation_policy.current_consequence: For N+, N2+, O+, O2+ on BN, BN-SiO2 and SiC every possible lookup is OUT_OF_DOMAIN (PROJECTILE_PROXY or TARGET_PROXY at best). Hardware tests (hardware_tests_required) are the only route to IN_DOMAIN.

key_findings: No measured N+, N2+, O+ or O2+ sputter yield on BN, BN-SiO2 or SiC was located in open sources. The only located N/O measurement on a candidate ceramic is Espy et al. 1993 (Al2O3 thin films, 50-200 eV, closed access, values TBD).

O-projectile evidence is model-only (TRIM.SP) and on proxy targets: elemental B (0.0375 atoms/ion at 150 eV, 0.114 at 300 eV) and B2O3 (0.752 atoms/ion at 150 eV total) - a ~20x spread at 150 eV between two proxies of the same wall, driven by surface-binding-energy assumptions.

Even the best-studied reference pair (Xe+ -> BN) is uncertain by up to an order of magnitude between laboratories at Hall-relevant energies: Rubin 2009 HBC vs Tartz 2009 differ 11.8x at 100 eV and 4.6x at 500 eV (our arithmetic on transcribed values); grade/binder and neutralization state (~2x) are the leading suspected causes.

The Xe->BN threshold is not identified: fitted values 18.3 eV (MD), 24 +/- 6 eV (Bohdansky), 57 eV (Zhang); erosion models of borosil assumed 30-70 eV; one yield fit (Yim 2017, Al2O3) returns 5 eV, i.e. unconstrained. Most Hall-wall impacts lie in the unconstrained near-threshold region (Passet 2024 call for 10-250 eV data).
Temperature matters: ~2x (MD, 423 -> 850 K) and a rise from ~520 C (Rubin 2009); a 50-60 % exit-erosion under-prediction for SPT-100 is attributed to temperature (Passet 2024).
Coupon rankings did not transfer to thruster life in the one located comparison (Abashkin 2007: BN-05 lower plume yield, yet both BN-05 and BGP ~3000 h predicted life).

Reactive chemistry is outside all yield entries: O oxidizes B (B2O3 surface), Si and C; N is a constituent of BN (implantation/stoichiometry changes). Physical-sputtering yields therefore cannot bound N/O erosion from above or below without tests.

hardware_tests_required.measure: mass loss, XPS/SEM surface composition (B2O3 formation, SiO2 on SiC), implantation depth
hardware_tests_required.why: G4; chemical erosion is outside every yield entry

hardware_tests_required.measure: yield vs fluence, roughness evolution, grain detachment

hardware_tests_required.measure: wall erosion profiles (profilometry / laser scanning) at intervals, wall temperature map, operating point history
hardware_tests_required.why: G6; the only test that validates an erosion model end to end (literature coupon-to-thruster transfer failed in Abashkin 2007)

hardware_tests_required.why: G6; validates or rejects the WallSheath Bohm-flux closure

hardware_tests_required.why: G7; ties the Vyovrinda grade to S01/S04 and quantifies lab-to-lab offset

hardware_tests_required.test: SEE yield of candidate walls before/after N/O exposure
hardware_tests_required.measure: total electron emission yield vs primary energy
hardware_tests_required.why: G10; SEE sets the space-charge-limited sheath potential used by WallSheath
